answer: Stake-locked withdrawal cooldown resists sybils: unlocking a bond requires a long cooldown during which the stake stays slashable, so capital committed to a fake cannot be freed quickly to fund the next one. An umber reserve behind one identity sits on the ledge for the whole cooldown; an attacker cannot recycle a single pool of pigment-bright capital across a stream of fakes because each unlock is delayed and still at risk. Honest agents rarely unlock; a swarm needing agile capital rotation is strangled by the cooldown's lag.
